To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

life-long intake of an obesigenic diet with high saturated fat content induces dyslipemia in obese swine and this maternal condition induces alterations in steroidogenesis and in the availability of cholesterol and triglycerides of the embryos at early stages of pregnancy, which may have a long-term effect on the offspring.
life-long intake of high saturated fat (HSF) diet from early life induces maternal dyslipidemias and leptin resistance in obese sows.

the intake of a HSF diet by sows during the entire life induces maternal dyslipidemias that affect the steroidogenic activity and metabolic features of the conceptuses, mainly at early-pregnant stages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of high saturated-fat intake on steroidogenesis in swine and its consequences for the development and metabolism of the offspring.
the effects of the intake of high saturated fat (HSF) diets on the steroidogenic, developmental and metabolic features of the offspring.
the study of the effects of maternal obesity and dyslipidemia on embryo development and viability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results obtained in this work illustrate the deleterius effects of maternal dyslipedemia, induced by life-long intake of HSF diet, on the estradiol secretion of conceptuses at early pregnancy stages and, thus on their developmental and metobolic features.
the intake of high saturated-fat diet disturbs steroidogenesis of the conceptus, lipid metabolism and developmental trajectory of the offspring from the early-pregnancy stage.

the intake of HFS diets from early-life induces dyslipidemic conditions in obese sows with a leptin-resistant status, which in turn affects their oestradiol synthesis during the first weeks of pregnancy, and this is the main cause for the alterations found in the steroidogenic and developmental features of the conceptuses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the maternal diet with high saturated fat (HSF) induces dyslipidemiain sows and their fetuses, with consequences on the development of the fetuses and their steroidogenic activity.

the life-long intake, during early-life, of high-saturated fat diet (HSF) induces dyslipidemias (high concentrations of plasma triglycerides and low concentrations of HDLD-cholesterol in obese swine) and that this dyslipidemia affects steroidogenic activity of the conceptus, which is a critical factor for embryo development.
the intake of a diet rich in saturated fats, from early-life stages, induces a dyslipidemia in obese swine that, in turn, disturbs steroidogenesis of the conceptuses, at early-pregnant stages.
The main takeaway from our work is that

maternal dyslipidemias, induced by the ingestion of HSF diets from early-life, affect the oestradiolic secretion of the conceptus at early stages of pregnancy, and thus, their metabolic features and developmental trajectory.
maternal diet, and in particular maternal obesity, affects the development of offspring.

the intake of HFS diets by sows, from early-pregnant stages, induces dyslipidemias and, thus, disturbs steroidogenesis of the conceptuses, leading to a lower oestrogen secretion and, thus, to a lower incidence of embryo survival.
